newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL- FINNISH YIELD GAP OVER GERMANY SEEN FALLING.
newsitem.headline: POLL- FINNISH YIELD GAP OVER GERMANY SEEN FALLING.

text.p: Finland's yield gap over
Germany is seen around 25 basis points in a month and 22 basis
points at the year-end -- lower if pay hikes are moderate and
EMU on track, a Reuter poll of seven operators on Wednesday
shows.
The gap stood at some 26 basis points on Wednesday, down
from 28 at Tuesday's close.
The mean of forecasts one-month ahead was 24.5 basis points
-- some operators saw strong support for the gap at 25 -- and
the mean by the end of the year was 21.8 basis points.
The range of forecasts one month ahead was 20 to 28 basis
points: the range by year-end was 15 to 35. But analysts with
higher estimates said their view would be more bullish if they
assumed moderate pay hikes for next year.
For instance, the one forecasting 35 basis points said the
gap would be 18 basis points if incomes settlement talks were to
follow the best possible scenario and lead to moderate pay
hikes. That would put the average at 19.4 basis points.
Forecasts for the Finnish 2006 yield gap over German
ten-year benchmark (basis points):
1-month ahead at year-end
Average 24.5 21.8
Highest 28.0 35.0
Lowest 20.0 15.0
The contributors to the poll were OKOBANK, Merita, Enskilda,
Handelsbanken, Interbank, Unibank and Postipankki.
